sections.skill: Define service scope, extras and deposits in writing

questions.prompt: Which scope statement is clearest?

choices.text: "Do whatever needs doing around the whole house"
"Deep clean of kitchen and 2 bathrooms; windows extra"

questions.correct_answer: "Deep clean of kitchen and 2 bathrooms; windows extra"
questions.intro: Service jobs go wrong when SCOPE is vague. Before starting, write what is included (for example "deep clean of kitchen and 2 bathrooms"), what is not ("windows and inside the oven are extra"), how many visits or revisions are included, and what happens with extras. Take a DEPOSIT for bookings or custom work, especially if you buy materials or reserve a date; state whether it is refundable. Confirm changes in writing before doing extra work.

questions.prompt: "Coloring extra" is like what in a scope?

choices.text: An item already included in the price

questions.correct_answer: An excluded item that costs more
questions.intro: A salon menu might say "Cut and style, 45 dollars; coloring extra; one free touch-up within 7 days." You know what you get and what costs more. If the stylist added coloring without asking and charged you, you would be upset. A service scope is the menu for one job: included work, extras, limits, and agreement before anything extra is done.
